stories.title: Real Assets Investment Veterans Launch One Orchard as New Platform
stories.excerpt: New York City-based One Orchard has launched as an investment firm and holding company designed to concentrate capital into fully integrated, proprietary real asset platforms. Concurrent with its launch, One Orchard is announcing its first investment and operating platform, InfraMed Properties, a healthcare infrastructure strategy focused on acquiring and managing critical medical outpatient facilities leased to leading healthcare systems and specialty care providers. InfraMed is seeded with a 25-asset portfolio and formed in partnership with REDICO, a vertically integrated real estate investment, development, and operating company with a 60-year track record and deep experience in healthcare. One Orchard’s investment in InfraMed is supported by its institutional limited partners, led by Pantheon, a leading global private markets investor with $84 billion in assets under management. David Elliott, One Orchard’s co-founder with Bradley Guz, said, “The formation of One Orchard and InfraMed is the culmination of our prior experiences investing over $10 billion in real assets and platforms over the past 15 years, and our strong view on the need for a more integrated approach in a new era of private markets and real assets investing.” The post Real Assets Investment Veterans Launch One Orchard as New Platform appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: One Orchard (NYC) launches with $84B LP Pantheon; seeded with healthcare real assets platform.
InfraMed Properties acquires/manages medical outpatient facilities; 25-asset portfolio partnered with REDICO.
Platform represents $10B+ in real assets deployed over 15 years; focused on integrated operating model.
stories.summary: One Orchard, a new NYC-based investment platform co-founded by David Elliott and Bradley Guz, has launched with backing from Pantheon (a $84 billion private markets investor) and announced its first platform, InfraMed Properties, which acquires and operates medical outpatient facilities leased to healthcare systems. InfraMed is seeded with a 25-asset portfolio in partnership with REDICO. The founders have deployed over $10 billion in real assets over 15 years and seek a more integrated operating approach in private markets.
stories.impact: Limited direct bearing on multifamily development. Healthcare real estate operates under different leasing dynamics, tenant credit profiles, and regulatory drivers than residential. No immediate signal for apartment market supply, demand, or capital availability.

stories.title: Grandbridge to Act as Servicer for $210M Refinancing of Two Seattle Office Towers
stories.excerpt: Grandbridge Real Estate Capital, a subsidiary of Truist, has been named master servicer on its first commercial mortgage-backed securities transaction, marking a significant milestone as the firm expands its servicing platform. Grandbridge will serve as master servicer for a $210 million refinancing of two office towers outside Seattle owned by Brookfield Asset Management. Goldman Sachs is providing an interest-only, fixed-rate mortgage loan with a four-year anticipated repayment date and a seven-year final maturity. Block 16 and 24 total 543,000 square feet and are within the transit-oriented Spring District, a 36-acre walkable neighborhood in Bellevue, Washington, which serves as a technology hub for the Pacific Northwest. Block 16 is an 11-story tower, while Block 24 is a 10-story building. Both are 100% leased, and tech giant Meta has occupied the Spring District since 2018. Brookfield Asset Management is a SASB issuer with approximately $1.1 trillion in assets under management. The post Grandbridge to Act as Servicer for $210M Refinancing of Two Seattle Office Towers appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Grandbridge (Truist subsidiary) named master servicer on $210M office refinance; Seattle/Bellevue, WA.
Brookfield Asset Management refinances two fully-leased towers (Block 16, 24); Meta occupant since 2018.
Spring District Bellevue tech hub; Goldman Sachs provides fixed-rate, interest-only, 4-yr amort/7-yr maturity loan.
stories.summary: Grandbridge Real Estate Capital, a Truist subsidiary, has been named master servicer on a $210 million CMBS refinancing of two 100%-leased office towers (543,000 SF total) in Bellevue's Spring District, a tech-anchored, transit-oriented neighborhood where Meta has been a major tenant since 2018. Goldman Sachs originated the fixed-rate, interest-only mortgage with a four-year anticipated repayment date and seven-year final maturity. This marks Grandbridge's first CMBS servicing role.
stories.impact: No direct multifamily impact. Office market refinancing activity, even in tech hubs, does not signal residential demand or supply shifts. Meta's continued Bellevue presence supports regional employment, but office leasing does not translate to apartment rental demand without broader corporate expansion or in-migration narratives.

stories.title: Realterm, Starwood Property Trust Co-Originate IOS Financing
stories.excerpt: Realterm, alongside Starwood Property Trust, Inc., announced the closing of a $672 million industrial outdoor storage (IOS) portfolio financing, the largest ever of its kind. The 78-property IOS portfolio is owned by affiliates of Stonemont Financial Group and Cerberus Capital Management and encompasses 830 acres of land across 33 U.S. markets. Eastdil Secured Savills arranged the transaction. “This financing marks a significant milestone for our credit platform and underscores our ability to execute sophisticated solutions that drive industry-making deals,” said Paul Sisson, Head of Credit at Realterm. “Borrowers are continuing to seek lenders with a deep understanding of the industrial real estate and logistics sectors.” Starwood manages a $32 million portfolio across its debt and equity investments. “Transactions like this one reflect the breadth and depth of Starwood’s commercial real estate lending platform,” said Jeffrey DiModica, President of Starwood Property Trust. The post Realterm, Starwood Property Trust Co-Originate IOS Financing appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Realterm, Starwood Property Trust co-originate $672M industrial outdoor storage financing; largest of its kind.
78-property portfolio across 33 U.S. markets; owned by Stonemont Financial and Cerberus Capital Management.
Portfolio spans 830 acres; Eastdil Secured Savills arranger; signals strong industrial debt appetite.
stories.summary: Realterm and Starwood Property Trust closed a $672 million co-originated financing for a 78-property industrial outdoor storage (IOS) portfolio owned by affiliates of Stonemont Financial Group and Cerberus Capital Management. The portfolio spans 830 acres across 33 U.S. markets. Eastdil Secured Savills arranged the transaction. Both lenders highlighted their deep industrial and logistics sector expertise and appetite for sophisticated credit solutions.
stories.impact: Indirect but positive signal: strong availability of debt capital for industrial real estate across diverse U.S. markets suggests credit conditions remain supportive of development and acquisition. However, no direct connection to multifamily demand or supply. Industrial financing strength does not compete for multifamily capital but indicates broader CRE lending health and lender risk appetite.

stories.title: JLL Arranges Sale of 1.1M-SF Subaru Distribution Facility in Indiana
stories.excerpt: JLL completed the sale of Subaru at Park 267, a 1,119,056-square-foot industrial distribution facility located at 5190 S. State Road 267 in Whitestown, Indiana. JLL represented the seller, a joint venture between Prologis and Browning, in the transaction. LaSalle Investment Management acquired the asset. The JLL Capital Markets Investment Sales and Advisory team was led by Senior Managing Director John Huguenard, Managing Director Ed Halaburt, Senior Director Ross Bratcher and Associate Cameron Chandra. The build-to-suit development was constructed by Browning’s construction division and completed in 2024. The facility is fully leased to Subaru of America Inc. and serves as the largest distribution center within its nine-facility national network. The property is strategically located 38.8 miles south of the tenant’s manufacturing facility in Lafayette, its sole production location outside of Asia. “Prologis and Browning delivered a best-in-class distribution facility that serves as a mission-critical component of the tenant’s North American supply chain,” Halaburt said. “The Indianapolis market’s robust absorption trends and limited new supply have created a highly competitive environment for institutional-quality assets with long-term cash flows.” The post JLL Arranges Sale of 1.1M-SF Subaru Distribution Facility in Indiana appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Subaru Park 267 (1.12M SF) in Whitestown, IN sold to LaSalle Investment Management by Prologis/Browning JV.
Build-to-suit completed 2024; fully-leased to Subaru; largest distribution center in Subaru's 9-facility network.
Indianapolis market shows strong absorption, limited new supply, and robust institutional investor interest.
stories.summary: JLL arranged the sale of Subaru at Park 267, a 1.12 million-square-foot industrial distribution facility in Whitestown, Indiana, completed in 2024 as a build-to-suit. LaSalle Investment Management acquired the asset from a Prologis-Browning joint venture. The facility is fully leased to Subaru of America and serves as its largest distribution center, strategically located 38.8 miles from Subaru's manufacturing facility in Lafayette.
stories.impact: Signals Indianapolis industrial market strength and institutional appetite for mission-critical logistics assets, but no direct multifamily implication. However, strong industrial absorption and limited new supply in Indianapolis could indirectly support warehouse-worker housing demand in secondary markets; monitor if Subaru or other logistics operators expand headcount regionally.

stories.title: New York City’s Technology Labor Market Has Surpassed San Francisco: Report
stories.excerpt: It’s official. New York is employing more tech workers than the San Francisco Bay area. According to an annual CBRE report on North American tech talent, the New York metropolitan area’s tech workforce reached 394,300 in 2025. The stat marks an 8.4 percent increase from 2022 that added 30,640 jobs. Meanwhile, San Francisco’s tech employment fell by 6 percent over the same period, totaling 375,730 jobs in 2025. This is the first time in the report’s 13-year history that the Big Apple has come out ahead. The city’s diversified job market helped set it apart, Colin Yasukochi, executive director of CBRE’s tech insights center, told Commercial Observer. “What really pushed New York past the San Francisco Bay Area has been the job reductions that we’ve seen [in San Francisco], with a lot of the announced layoffs, and the fact that New York has continued to grow,” Yasukochi said. San Francisco remains in North America’s top spot for its pool of tech talent, however, ranked across 13 metrics. The report, which analyzed the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics and LinkedIn data, found that tech jobs make up more than 10 percent of total employment in San Francisco, compared to just 4.2 percent in New York. But a whopping 61 percent of San Francisco’s tech talent works directly in the tech industry, according to CBRE’s report, leaving its general labor market vulnerable. In New York City, just 34 percent of its tech workers work within the industry, while 21 percent work in tech roles in finance, insurance and real estate industries (otherwise known as FIRE). “[That] has given New York resilience from the tech downturn that broadly started in 2022, in terms of employment,” Yasukochi said. “But, obviously, with the artificial intelligence industry coming into play, that’s turned around quite substantially in the last year.” Yasukochi added that New York also benefits from a massive university infrastructure and lower wages than San Francisco, on average, for
bullets: NYC tech employment reached 394,300 in 2025; +8.4% since 2022; surpassed San Francisco for first time.
San Francisco tech jobs fell 6% to 375,730 over same period; NYC added 30,640 jobs.
NYC's diversified job market and SF layoffs drove divergence; report covers 13-year historical series.
stories.summary: According to CBRE's annual North American tech talent report, New York City's tech workforce reached 394,300 in 2025, a gain of 30,640 jobs (+8.4%) since 2022 and marking the first time in the report's 13-year history that NYC has surpassed San Francisco's tech employment. San Francisco's tech jobs fell 6% to 375,730 over the same period, driven by announced layoffs and slower growth. NYC's diversified job market helped differentiate it from the Bay Area's tech concentration.
stories.impact: Strong positive signal for NYC multifamily demand, particularly in Manhattan, Brooklyn, and transit-accessible areas (LIC, Astoria, etc.) where tech workers cluster. Net 30,640+ new tech jobs in NYC metro over 3 years signals sustained in-migration, higher renter incomes, and rent growth potential. Developers should prioritize transit-oriented, amenity-rich projects in secondary submarkets capturing tech talent spillover from Manhattan; acquisition windows narrowing in core submarkets as cap rates reflect demand.

stories.title: Texas People & Companies, August 21, 2026
stories.excerpt: Dallas-based Mohr Partners named Kam Schroeder as President of Brokerage, a newly created role designed to support the expansion of the firm’s national brokerage platform. Schroeder brings extensive corporate real estate experience to Mohr Partners, most recently serving as Executive Vice President and Managing Director of Newmark’s East Bay brokerage operations. Prior to Newmark, he was Senior Vice President at Hughes Marino and spent more than a decade at JLL and its predecessor, The Staubach Company. Dallas-based Apricus Realty Capital acquired 8799 Crownhill Blvd., a 53,100-square-foot IOS property situated on approximately 4.3 acres in San Antonio. Located immediately adjacent to San Antonio International Airport, the asset features a combination of crane-served warehouse space, maintenance facilities, a concrete storage yard and multiple drive-in loading positions designed to accommodate fleet, construction and industrial users. Stream Realty Partners has been awarded the leasing assignment for Valley Ridge 35, a two-building Class A industrial development in Lewisville, Texas. Developed by Crow Holdings Development in partnership with Lewisville Development, LP, the project is scheduled to deliver in June 2027. Located along Valley Ridge Boulevard with direct access to Interstate 35, Valley Ridge 35 will offer 329,651 square feet of industrial space across two rear-load buildings. Sarah Ozanne and Mac Hall will lead leasing efforts on behalf of the ownership. EōS Fitness secured a 40,000-square-foot retail lease in the Grand Parkway Center, facilitated by NewQuest. Located at the prime super-regional intersection of Highway 99/Grand Parkway and State Highway 249, it’s projected to open in 2027. Based in Dallas, EōS Fitness has 33 open locations across Houston, the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex and San Antonio, with plans to expand into Austin in the near term. stories.title: Principal Financial Group Loans $32M to Refi Queens Shopping Center
stories.excerpt: An affiliate of Mattone Investors secured $32 million to refinance Springnex Plaza, a 96,028-square-foot shopping center anchored by a Stop & Shop supermarket in the Queens neighborhood of Springfield Gardens. Principal Financial Group provided the debt, while Northmarq’s Robert Delitsky and Charles Cotsalas arranged the transaction. Delitsky noted in a statement that Mattone Investors first developed Springnex Plaza six years ago and “have done a fabulous job maintaining very strong occupancy” since then. “Supermarket-anchored shopping centers like Springnex Plaza will continue to attract very strong lender interest in today’s market,” Cotsalas added in the same statement. Located at 134-40 Springfield Boulevard, Springnex Plaza sits on 5.58 acres of land and is 100 percent occupied. Besides Stop & Shop, tenants include an IHOP, fashion retailer Ashley Stewart and Northwell Health GoHealth Urgent Care. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Principal Financial Group provided $32M refi for Springnex Plaza, Springfield Gardens, Queens; 100% occupied.
96,028-SF shopping center anchored by Stop & Shop; 5.58 acres; developed by Mattone Investors 6 years prior.
Supermarket-anchored retail continues to attract strong lender interest in today's lending environment.
stories.summary: An affiliate of Mattone Investors secured $32 million from Principal Financial Group to refinance Springnex Plaza, a 96,028-square-foot, fully-occupied shopping center in Springfield Gardens, Queens, anchored by Stop & Shop. The 5.58-acre property, developed by Mattone six years ago, also houses IHOP, Ashley Stewart, and a Northwell Health GoHealth Urgent Care. Northmarq arranged the transaction and noted sustained lender appetite for supermarket-anchored retail.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily. Retail refinancing and lender appetite do not signal apartment demand or capital competition. However, strong Queens retail fundamentals (100% occupancy, supermarket anchor, healthcare co-tenant) suggest underlying population stability and local purchasing power in Springfield Gardens—a data point for residential submarkets in outer Queens, but not a demand driver.

stories.title: Data Center Development Has Domestic Materials Manufacturers Working Overtime
stories.excerpt: Development in the U.S. saw spotty progress in the first half of 2026 with costs of materials continuing to climb and asset classes with only the highest returns being built. That means data centers, power infrastructure, advanced manufacturing and pharmaceutical production are taking off, while office, retail and higher education on a national level lag way behind, due, in large part, to President Donald Trump’s ongoing tariff policies, according to a Skanska report. But just because there is a lull in some sectors does not mean supply chains for materials aren’t working at full capacity, Tom Park, vice president of national strategic supply chain at Skanska, told Commercial Observer. “The market is hot and cold right now — hot and warm may be a better way to say it — so what stands out is that we’re seeing a lot of project activity around data centers, semiconductor, life sciences,” Park said in an interview. “There’s really a lot of unprecedented demand in the mechanical, electrical, plumbing and steel space driving up lead times and cost.” Some factors causing these supply chain hemorrhages are Section 338 tariffs on Canada, delays on petrochemical import ships through the Strait of Hormuz, and domestic materials priced higher simply because of the supply and demand constraints. Tariffs on steel, aluminum and copper in particular are driving prices up. “What happens with tariffs is that it really raises the opportunity for domestic producers to raise their prices,” Park said. “For steel, aluminum and copper, the tariffs really have increased pricing on all those materials and derivative products because the foreign competition obviously has that tariff to overcome.” Lead times for material deliveries have increased from 24 to 36 weeks to 40 to 50 weeks, indicating to Park that metal mills and fabricators are running at full capacity. bullets: U.S. construction costs rising due to Trump tariff policies; data centers, semiconductors, life sciences accelerating.
Office, retail, higher education lag due to material cost pressure; mechanical, electrical, plumbing, steel lead times and costs climbing.
Skanska reports spotty sectoral progress in H1 2026; only highest-return asset classes justify development.
stories.summary: According to a Skanska report, U.S. construction development in H1 2026 has been uneven due to rising material costs driven by tariff policies. Data centers, semiconductors, power infrastructure, and life sciences are accelerating, while office, retail, and higher education lag. Mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and steel supply chains are working at full capacity, driving up lead times and costs across sectors with strong project activity.
stories.impact: Moderately negative for multifamily development. Rising construction costs and extended lead times for MEP and steel reduce project feasibility and compress margins on standard apartment communities, particularly in markets without rent premiums. Multifamily developers may face cost inflation without corresponding rent growth unless targeting high-barrier-to-entry, dense urban infill or tech-growth metros. Monitor tariff policy changes; short-term headwinds favor only best-in-class, high-return projects in constrained-supply submarkets.

stories.title: Azora, Vizcaya Capital Flip Coconut Grove Office Building for $62M
stories.excerpt: Just a year after buying a boutique office building in Miami’s coveted Coconut Grove neighborhood, Azora Private Solutions and Vizcaya Capital sold it for a nearly $15 million gain. The five-story property at 3250 Mary Street, called the Grove at 3250 Mary, sold for $62.3 million, according to the brokers who represented the sellers, Berkadia’s Omar Morales and Jaret Turkell. The joint venture had purchased the 80,000-square-foot building for $47.5 million last September. Records show the buyer is an entity tied to El-Ad National Properties, the Boca Raton-based division of Israeli billionaire Isaac Tshuva’s El-Ad Group. “Coconut Grove continues to distinguish itself as one of South Florida’s strongest real estate markets, driven by exceptional demand from luxury residential buyers and high-net-worth office users,” Morales said in a statement. “That demand, combined with limited supply, continues to attract remarkable investment to the neighborhood.” In recent years, Coconut Grove has attracted a slew of billionaires, including Google’s billionaire founder Larry Page, who spent about $170 million assembling a residential compound last year. The residential acquisitions have fueled demand for luxury office space nearby. The acquisition of the 1982-built, 1.3-acre site office building marks somewhat of a deviation for El-Ad National, which has typically focused on residential and mixed-use development. It also comes just four months after the developer purchased a nearby, low-rise condo building for $45.5 million, which will likely be redeveloped. Earlier this month, up north in Fort Lauderdale, the firm bought an oceanfront hotel for $60 million. A representative for El-Ad Group was not immediately available for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialoserver.com.
bullets: Azora/Vizcaya Capital flipped Grove at 3250 Mary, Miami Coconut Grove, for $62.3M; ~$15M gain in 1 year.
Purchased $47.5M Sept 2024; sold to El-Ad National Properties (Israeli billionaire Tshuva's U.S. division).
Coconut Grove office market driven by luxury residential buyers, high-net-worth office users, and limited supply.
stories.summary: Azora Private Solutions and Vizcaya Capital sold the Grove at 3250 Mary, an 80,000-square-foot, five-story office building in Miami's Coconut Grove, for $62.3 million, roughly $15 million above their September 2024 purchase price of $47.5 million. The buyer is an entity affiliated with El-Ad National Properties, the U.S. division of Israeli billionaire Isaac Tshuva's El-Ad Group. Market brokers cited Coconut Grove's appeal to luxury residential buyers and high-net-worth office users, combined with limited supply.
stories.impact: Signals strong Miami office market dynamics but not multifamily-specific. However, Coconut Grove's emergence as a destination for billionaires and ultra-high-net-worth individuals (Google founder noted) suggests underlying amenity and lifestyle appeal that could drive adjacent multifamily demand in walkable, mixed-use Coconut Grove and nearby Wynwood/Midtown submarkets. Monitor for residential conversions or new luxury multifamily development in Coconut Grove as office market tightens.

stories.title: Affinius Capital Lends $177M for Multifamily Asset Buy in New Jersey, Yonkers
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between Lincoln Property Company, Saber-Hightower and Waterfall Asset Management has sealed $177.25 million of acquisition financing for the purchase of two multifamily properties in the New York metropolitan area, Commercial Observer has learned. Affinus Capital provided the debt package for the sponsorship’s purchase of the 262-unit Edgewater Harbor property in Edgewater, N.J., and the soon-to-be completed 147-unit Trilogy Lofts at Tuckahoe project in Yonkers, N.Y. The deal involved a $124 million loan for Edgewater Harbor and $53.4 million of acquisition debt for Trilogy Lofts. The joint venture of Lincoln Property Company, Saber-Hightower and Waterfall Asset Management acquired both properties from National Resources as part of a $450 million acquisition of four tri-state region properties encompassing more than 4 million square feet, CO previously first reported. “Edgewater and Trilogy Lofts represent a compelling opportunity to invest in high-quality, well-located multifamily assets in supply-constrained, transit-oriented submarkets with durable renter demand,” David Greenburg, managing director at Affinius Capital, said in a statement. “Waterfall Asset Management, Lincoln Property Company and Saber-Hightower bring institutional scale, local market expertise, and a proven track record of value-add execution that positions this portfolio for long-term performance.” Cushman & Wakefield negotiated the financing with a team consisting of John Alascio, Alex Hernandez, Brad Domenico, Chuck Kohaut and Mitch Rothstein. C&W also represented the seller in the acquisition with a Northeast capital markets team of Andy Merin, Frank DiTommaso and Ryan Dowd. Located at 45 River Road 6 miles from Midtown Manhattan, Edgewater Harbor features 60,500 square feet of retail space anchored by a Sprouts Farmers Market slated to open in 2027. bullets: Affinius Capital provided $177.25M acquisition financing for JV (Lincoln, Saber-Hightower, Waterfall); tri-state multifamily.
Financed Edgewater Harbor (262 units, Edgewater, NJ; $124M) + Trilogy Lofts (147 units, Yonkers, NY; $53.4M).
Part of $450M acquisition by JV of four tri-state properties (~4M SF); transit-oriented, supply-constrained submarkets.
stories.summary: A joint venture of Lincoln Property Company, Saber-Hightower, and Waterfall Asset Management secured $177.25 million in acquisition financing from Affinius Capital for two multifamily assets: the 262-unit Edgewater Harbor in Edgewater, New Jersey ($124 million), and the 147-unit Trilogy Lofts at Tuckahoe in Yonkers, New York ($53.4 million). The two properties are part of a larger $450 million acquisition from National Resources encompassing four tri-state properties totaling over 4 million square feet.
stories.impact: Positive signal for tri-state multifamily capital availability and investor appetite for supply-constrained, transit-oriented assets. Yonkers and Edgewater NJ are affordable-to-moderate alternatives to Manhattan; strong financing on new/near-completion units indicates lender confidence in suburban NY/NJ rental demand. This supports developer thesis in Hudson Valley, Northern NJ, and Westchester County markets. Monitor acquisitions—if major operators are consolidating tri-state assets, cap rates likely rising, signaling window closing for new-build development in these submarkets.
